findings.claim: Snapshot streams expose a resumable checkpoint in the Accepted frame before delivering the snapshot rows it covers, allowing a client that disconnects after Accepted to resume after the snapshot cursor and permanently miss the snapshot payload.
findings.evidence: In the Snapshot branch, `last_offset` is set from `snapshot.cursor.as_ref().map(|cursor| cursor.broker_offset)` and `initial` contains the snapshot rows plus SnapshotComplete; immediately afterwards `accepted_frame(&request, &scope, last_offset, &initial)` is pushed before `frames.extend(initial)`. `accepted_frame` issues `start_checkpoint` from that `last_offset`, so the first frame can contain a checkpoint at the snapshot barrier before any `SnapshotRow` has been delivered. Acceptance criterion 4 requires reconnect/resume to meet the contract.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not issue a barrier/resume checkpoint in `Accepted` for snapshot starts; either omit/zero the accepted checkpoint for snapshots or issue only a pre-snapshot checkpoint, and make the first resumable snapshot-barrier checkpoint appear in `SnapshotComplete` after all snapshot rows have been sent.

findings.claim: The recorded acceptance evidence is internally inconsistent about the test-log hash, so the source-bound runtime proof is not a matching receipt.
findings.evidence: `acceptance-a.md` records `Test-log SHA-256: 84f09dd5ab14ca51e843c15b3fc281edd41351b1e06dda6cddbf74c712836626`, while `runtime-receipt.json` for the same run `20260916201305-51548` records `sha256.testLog` as `796320f9a409d6fe0d18dae53cace55bbc223ec8d57236be9d460bb28c29b9ab`. Acceptance criterion 5 requires a source-bound receipt, and the spec scenario says missing or stale matching fingerprints keep the gate open.
findings.suggested_fix: Regenerate or correct the evidence so all files for run `20260916201305-51548` reference the same test-log artifact hash, or include separate receipts if they are different artifacts.
